For each pair of facets, a point with exactly the pair tight proves a ridge except in four narrow cases when p=2 or q=2; those force at least one independent third equality. Thus R=C(pq+p+q,2)−[pq1_{q=2}+pq1_{p=2}+C(p,2)1_{q=2}+C(q,2)1_{p=2}]. Outward normals have magnitudes 1,√q,√p with only incident Z-row/column products −1 and row-column +1, giving stated acute, right, and obtuse angles and multiplicities. The mean follows directly, is obtuse only p=q=2 with π/2+π/27; Taylor expansion in square n gives deficit 4n^(−5/2).
